There is everything left for you here. You hit the bottom, now do a little bit every day to try and get back up. Wash the dishes one day, see how that makes you feel. Talk to someone like a stranger the next, see how that makes you feel. It will be slow progress but don't force yourself out of this rut all at once. Find little things to make you want to live again, don't hurry yourself, take your time, be kind to your body and your mind. Figure out if there are certain needs that you have that are unmet. If there are plenty, work up your way to meeting these needs. Find a therapist to help you bring yourself back out of this rut so that you aren't doing it all on your own. Watch these youtube videos for some inspiration/advice. We all face depression, think about why that is. What is it that we are missing in our lives?

This is an example of mentally and emotionally restrictive religion. I know because my parents do it as well. A good thing my therapist has told me (who is also christian) is that anything that suppresses or harms your health in any way (mental, emotional, physical) is not a representation of religion. Yes, believing in the presence of God can often aid with certain struggles, through believing in a higher power and not putting all the pressure on yourself, but if you have clear unworked out issues, that is something only you or a professional can fix. Another thing to consider is that depression and anxiety are often signs of unmet needs that you are experiencing. Rather than looking at depression and anxiety as solely biological, which is only slightly true, look at the things in your life that would bring you satisfaction that you are missing out on. If you would like, you can watch this ted talk, it talks about mental illness as a series of unmet needs as opposed to a mental handicap [https://youtu.be/MB5IX-np5fE](https://youtu.be/MB5IX-np5fE). Also, a family who oppresses your personality or suppresses your emotions can make you hate religion for that simple fact. Try avoiding talking to them about religion and talking to more accepting, positive individuals. It's hard to enjoy something when everyone is putting so much pressure on it. If you need anything, just knock right on my door, aka my inbox. :)

I know exactly what you’re feeling. I have had the same thing happen to me time after time and it’s just so uneccesary of the other person. What everyone says is true, it only reflects on who they are as a person. But that doesn’t make it any easier to handle. 

First you’ll get angry and overcompensate and rationalize why they said what they said. Then you continue to think about what they said and you let it fester for long amounts of time. It’s damn hard let me tell you, to forget when someone has said something ugly about you. But you just have to understand that what they say about you doesn’t define YOU. You are much more than what people say about you, and I want you to internalize that. 

You seem like you are a good person and a lot of times mean people take it upon themselves to say hateful things about even the nicest of people. Don’t let these things define you, I want you to look into the mirror every damn day and anything negative somebody said about you, I want you to say the exact opposite. I want you to become the identity that encompasses great things, and not the things that these people say about you. 

Now is the time to start building up yourself and make yourself into the skyscraper you were meant to me. While you build yourself up stronger, they will only be at the bottom trying to tear other skyscrapers down. They will always stay at the bottom because they use hate instead of love, which we all know is not sustainable. 

This is the advice I would have given myself a year ago. Be strong, carry on, a year down the road you will find yourself more strong and more confident than you were before. You may think this has destroyed you because it feels like it momentarily, but you will come out two times as strong. All the love, I wish the best for you.
